samples.summary: Removing the preview weight clamp makes "Dashed" render as a fully solid line at the largest border weight
samples.evidence: `StrokePreview` now draws into a fixed 64px-wide box (`PREVIEW_W = 64`) with `pattern = dashArray(dash, width)`. At width 16, `dashArray('dashed', 16)` = `[96, 64]` — the first dash alone (96px) is longer than the entire 64px preview line, so the Dashed row in the dash menu (border-picker.tsx:208, fed `value?.width`) and the 16px row in the weight menu (border-picker.tsx:175) paint an unbroken line, indistinguishable from Solid. Dotted at 16 gives `[32,32]`, i.e. one dash and one gap. The canvas is fine because shapes are far wider than 64px, but the picker — whose whole job is to distinguish the three dash styles — now shows the same drawing for two different choices. The deleted `DASH_PREVIEW_MAX_WEIGHT` was what prevented this; nothing replaced it (e.g. scaling the pattern to the preview length).

samples.summary: Connector dash is now imported but still never exported, so a dashed connector loses its dash on PPTX export
samples.evidence: `parseCxnSp` resolves its stroke through `parseShapeStroke` (import/pptx/shape.ts:1054), which this change taught to read `<a:prstDash>` — so an imported connector now carries `dash`. The connector exporter builds its own line element without any `prstDash`: `const ln = `<a:ln w="${lnW}">${fillXml}${headXml}${tailXml}</a:ln>`` (export/pptx/connector.ts:110); it does not go through `lineXml`, which is the only place `DASH_VAL`/`<a:prstDash>` is emitted (export/pptx/shape.ts:153). Result: import a deck with a dashed connector (or set a dash on a connector in the toolbar), export, and the dash is silently dropped — the exact asymmetry the new shape round-trip test closes for shapes only. The new round-trip case (test/export/pptx/round-trip.test.ts:241) covers shapes, not connectors, so nothing catches it.
searchedFor: grep parseShapeStroke call sites in packages/slides/src/import

samples.summary: Table cell borders still drop `dash` on both import and export while the renderer now scales their dash by width
samples.evidence: `paintCellBorders` was updated to `dashArray(edge.stroke.dash, edge.stroke.width)` (view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:314) and `CellBorder` has a `dash?` field (model/element.ts:435), but `parseCellBorder` returns `{ color, width }` with no dash (import/pptx/table.ts:223) and the table exporter writes `<a:ln${side} w=...>${solidFillXml(color)}</a:ln${side}>` with no `<a:prstDash>` (export/pptx/table.ts:120). Dashed table borders from PowerPoint therefore still import as solid and any model-side dash is lost on export — the same defect this change fixes for shapes, left unfixed for tables.
searchedFor: grep prstDash across packages/slides/src/export and src/import

finding.summary: Removing the preview weight clamp makes "Dashed" render as a fully solid line at the largest border weight
finding.evidence: `StrokePreview` now draws into a fixed 64px-wide box (`PREVIEW_W = 64`) with `pattern = dashArray(dash, width)`. At width 16, `dashArray('dashed', 16)` = `[96, 64]` — the first dash alone (96px) is longer than the entire 64px preview line, so the Dashed row in the dash menu (border-picker.tsx:208, fed `value?.width`) and the 16px row in the weight menu (border-picker.tsx:175) paint an unbroken line, indistinguishable from Solid. Dotted at 16 gives `[32,32]`, i.e. one dash and one gap. The canvas is fine because shapes are far wider than 64px, but the picker — whose whole job is to distinguish the three dash styles — now shows the same drawing for two different choices. verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out in the repo. stroke-preview.tsx:5 fixes the preview line at PREVIEW_W = 64 and stroke-preview.tsx:41 applies the unclamped pattern `dashArray(dash, width)` to a line spanning x=0..64 (stroke-preview.tsx:57-66). render-context.ts:99-102 returns [6*w, 4*w] for 'dashed', so at width 16 the pattern is [96, 64] — the first dash alone exceeds the entire 64px preview, producing an unbroken stroke identical to the Solid row (which omits stroke-dasharray). This is reachable in normal use: border-picker.tsx:44 offers 16 as a selectable weight, border-picker.tsx:208 feeds `value?.width` into the Dashed row, and border-picker.tsx:175 feeds `value?.dash` into the 16px weight row. Grep confirms DASH_PREVIEW_MAX_WEIGHT no longer exists in any source file (only prose at render-context.ts:78 and docs), and nothing scales the pattern to the preview length. The nearest refutation ground would be 'out-of-scope' on docs/design/slides/slides-toolbar-redesign.md:187-195, which accepts the tradeoff — but that same section states the preview's purpose is that it "cannot drift from what the canvas paints" (:179-182), and a 16px dashed border on a real shape does show dashes while the 64px preview shows solid, so the drift the design exists to prevent is exactly what occurs. Not refutable with confidence; the picker showing one drawing for two different choices is a real wrong-result bug on a reachable path.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. parseCxnSp resolves connector stroke via the same parseShapeStroke that now reads <a:prstDash> (import/pptx/shape.ts:1024-1026, 1054, 1070), and ConnectorElement.stroke is a ShapeStroke with dash (model/connector.ts:33, model/element.ts:163). The connector exporter hand-builds its line as `<a:ln w="${lnW}">${fillXml}${headXml}${tailXml}</a:ln>` (export/pptx/connector.ts:110) with no dash term, and it is the only connector serializer (sole call site export/pptx/group.ts:71). The single producer of <a:prstDash> in the whole package is lineXml (export/pptx/shape.ts:151-157), whose only call sites are export/pptx/shape.ts:198 and :243 — never connector.ts; DASH_VAL is module-private. A repo-wide search for `a:ln w=` in .ts sources yields only those two producers, so no indirect/post-processing path re-adds the dash. The state is real and rendered (connector-renderer.ts:50 setLineDash from stroke.dash), so a dashed connector imported from PPTX exports back as solid — silent loss of a fidelity attribute on a normal round-trip path. Connector export tests assert only color/width (test/export/pptx/connector.test.ts:65-75), so nothing catches it.
